notes: §1985:VII.2.7.4 GR6: for an external file connector 'all PADDING CHARACTER clauses in the run unit which are associated with that file connector must have the same specifications. If data-name-1 is specified, it must reference an external data item' (with §1985:VII.2.3.4 GR1g 'The same specification for the PADDING CHARACTER clause'). ExternalFileConnectorRules.Check, over the compilation group, refuses a non-external data-name-1 of an external file (COBOL1624, the witness) and compares FileEntryIdentity.Segments' PAD segment (literal-1's character, or data-name-1's external item identity, captured by CapturePadding and resolved in ResolveFiles) across entries, reporting COBOL6847. Probes at --std 85, two programs of one run unit (work-rd-04/c4): "*" vs "#" refused; "*" vs "*" and QUOTE vs QUOTES accepted and the file written by one program is read by the other (PB AAAA); the clause in one entry only ("*" or SPACE) refused, as GR1g asks the same specification of every entry; the same external PADC in both accepted; PADC vs literal, PADC vs a different external PADD, and PADC OF an external group vs another external PADC refused; a non-external file with a non-external data-name accepted and runs; the clause is refused at 2014 (COBOL0902, edition arm).

next.reason: 1985: "all PADDING CHARACTER clauses in the run unit which are associated with that file connector must have the same specifications"; 2023: "No PADDING CHARACTER clause in the candidates; the external file control entry consistency list (GR-12.4.5.3-1 a-m) omits it". No 2023 clause holds the PADDING CHARACTER feature. The external-file consistency rules for file control entries list other clauses but not PADDING CHARACTER.
